messages.author: alice
messages.content: morning all — deploying checkout-api v2.3 this morning, mostly the worker-concurrency bump we discussed

messages.author: bob
messages.content: v2.3 raises gunicorn worker concurrency from 8 to 32 per pod to cut queue time. each worker keeps its own Postgres connection pool though — worth watching DB connections

messages.author: alice
messages.content: noted. max_connections on the primary is 100. should be fine at current pod count

messages.author: deploybot
messages.content: DEPLOY: checkout-api v2.3 rolled out to production at 16:10 UTC (8 pods)

messages.author: pagerduty
messages.content: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: checkout-api p99 latency 3200ms (threshold 800ms). On-call paged.

messages.author: bob
messages.content: 5xx rate on checkout-api climbing too, around 12% of requests now. started ~16:50

messages.author: alice
messages.content: DB dashboard: Postgres active connections pegged at 100/100 (max_connections), lots of backends in 'idle in transaction' and a growing wait queue

messages.author: bob
messages.content: timing lines up with the v2.3 rollout at 16:10 — we bumped worker concurrency 4x. 8 pods × 32 workers each holding pool connections blows way past 100

messages.author: carol
messages.content: yeah — so checkout requests are stuck waiting for a free DB connection, that's the latency and the 5xx. classic connection pool exhaustion after the concurrency change

messages.author: alice
messages.content: agreed on cause. mitigation: rolling back checkout-api to v2.2 now to drop concurrency back to 8

messages.author: deploybot
messages.content: DEPLOY: checkout-api rolled back to v2.2 at 17:03 UTC

messages.author: bob
messages.content: rollback applied. active DB connections dropping (now ~55/100), p99 back under 700ms, 5xx clearing

messages.author: carol
messages.content: confirmed recovered. we still want the v2.3 concurrency win — follow-up is to cap per-worker pool size (e.g. pgbouncer) or raise max_connections before re-deploying
